claims.proposition: Imut-imut means sweet, small, and endearing.
DBP defines comel in relation to attractive children and small, attractive animals.
Indonesian imut and Malaysian comel are common words for an endearing, cute appearance.

context.scope: Contemporary everyday descriptions of people, objects, and conditions; avoid polysemous cues unless disambiguated

source_leads.exact_claim: The entry defines imut-imut as manis, mungil, dan menggemaskan.

claims.proposition: Capek means tired or lacking energy.
Capek is a conversational Indonesian form associated with Jakarta speech; lelah is an alternative.
DBP defines penat as feeling unable to continue and needing rest, and gives letih as a synonym.
Indonesian capek and Malaysian penat are common everyday words for feeling tired and needing rest.

context.scope: Contemporary everyday descriptions of people, objects, and conditions; avoid polysemous cues unless disambiguated

source_leads.exact_claim: The entry glosses capek as tidak bertenaga/berkekuatan lagi; lelah.
The entry labels cape Jk and glosses it as lelah, letih, capai.

claims.proposition: Keras kepala describes a person who will not follow others' advice.
DBP defines degil as unwilling to follow what one is told or accept advice, and lists keras kepala as an equivalent.
Indonesian keras kepala and Malaysian degil commonly describe someone unwilling to heed advice or change their position.

context.scope: Contemporary everyday descriptions of people, objects, and conditions; avoid polysemous cues unless disambiguated

source_leads.exact_claim: The entry glosses keras kepala as tidak mau menurut nasihat orang and lists kepala batu.

claims.proposition: Rusak can describe an object that is no longer intact or a machine that no longer works.
DBP includes damaged objects and a vehicle that no longer runs among the senses of rosak.
Indonesian rusak and Malaysian rosak both describe damaged objects or objects that no longer work.

context.scope: Contemporary everyday descriptions of people, objects, and conditions; avoid polysemous cues unless disambiguated

source_leads.exact_claim: The entry includes senses sudah tidak sempurna (baik, utuh) lagi and tidak dapat berjalan lagi for a car or machine.

claims.proposition: Lapar means feeling a desire to eat because the stomach is empty.
DBP defines lapar as wanting to eat because the stomach is empty.
Lapar is the common word for wanting food in both Indonesian and Malaysian Malay.

context.scope: Contemporary everyday descriptions of people, objects, and conditions; avoid polysemous cues unless disambiguated

source_leads.exact_claim: The dictionary defines lapar as berasa ingin makan karena perutnya kosong.

claims.proposition: DBP gives tidak kotor, meaning free of dirt, as the first sense of bersih.
Bersih is the common word for being free of dirt in both Indonesian and Malaysian Malay.

context.scope: Contemporary everyday descriptions of people, objects, and conditions; avoid polysemous cues unless disambiguated

source_leads.exact_claim: The entry's first sense defines bersih as bebas dari kotoran.

prompt:
# Audit external evidence (prompt set 1.0.0)

Independently inspect every proposed source or corpus result. A model citation, URL, or dictionary
entry by itself is only a lead. For each observation, state exactly which claim is supported,
contradicted, or left inconclusive. Record the access method, page location or reproducible query,
short observed content, access time, publisher, underlying source group, locale, register, and
limitations. Count mirrors and copied pages as one underlying source. A dictionary listing proves
existence or a sense, not normal everyday preference by itself. Report contrary evidence.

Return JSON only: `{"schema_version":1,"role":"evidence-audit","model":"MODEL/TOOL",
"result":{"observations":[{"evidence_id":"...","claim_id":"...","source_group":"...",
"source_title":"...","publisher":"...","url_or_query":"...","accessed_at":"ISO UTC",
"observation":"...","page_location_or_query":"...",
"audit_method":"retrieved-page|corpus-query|manual-inspection",
"stance":"supports|contradicts|inconclusive","claim_type":"meaning|locale-usage|preferred-choice|relation|misleading-contrast",
"usage_basis":"contextual|comparative|dictionary-only","locale":"...","register":"...",
"limitations":"..."}]}}`.
If a source cannot be inspected, omit it from supporting observations and report the failure.
